question: A 49-year-old male complains of abdominal discomfort that worsens following meals. A gastric biopsy reveals a 2 cm gastric ulcer, and immunohistochemical staining demonstrates the presence of a rod-shaped bacterium in the gastric mucosa. Which of the following is used by the infiltrating pathogen to neutralize gastric acidity?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Presence of rod-shaped bacterium in gastric mucosa" -> "Pathogen uses urease to neutralize gastric acidity" -> 95% CHAIN: "Gastric ulcer identified on biopsy" -> "Pathogen secretes urease to survive in the acidic environment" -> 90% CHAIN: "Immunohistochemical staining shows rod-shaped bacterium" -> "Pathogen produces urease to counteract gastric acidity" -> 95%
analysis: The presence of a rod-shaped bacterium in the gastric mucosa along with a gastric ulcer suggests infection with Helicobacter pylori. H. pylori uses urease to neutralize gastric acidity by converting urea to ammonia, which helps the bacteria survive in the acidic environment of the stomach.
